text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Four major demands from Nigeria will top agenda of two-day talks Tuesday aand Wednesday with visiting Commonwealth ministers. They are lifting suspension of Nigeria from Commonwealth, no more threat of sanctions, support for military leader Sani Abacha's transition to democracy programme and talks between Nigeria and Commonwealth at highest level.
- Nigerian Telecommunications Ltd orders 30,000 telephone boxes for installation in Ikeja and Apapa districts of Lagos, spokesman says
- Oil firms in Nigeria must henceforth pay hard currency to renew operating licences when they expire, officials say.
- Nigeria has 250 million tonnes of marble reserves, says head of Jakura Marble Industry Ltd.
- Central bank proposes that government should raise minimum equity capital of banks to 500 million naira from the current 50 million to strengthen their bases.
- Local councils are henceforth to receive their federal revenue directly from the central bank rather than through state governments, says federal accountant-general M.A. Argungu.
- Lacking technical expertise to exploit their oil fields, indigenous firms farm out their deepwater blocks to local units of Mobil Corp and Texaco Inc, industry sources say.
- Researchers at central bank call for independence for the Apex Bank.
